content:
Maria: Heads-up: saw a flurry of Xid errors last night in us-west-2; ops reported ~12 noisy cards. Traceback collection was sparse. Proposal: add prioritized dmesg/journalctl/nvidia-smi snippets on GPU drain and on Xid/ECC events so we can triage faster.

Kevin: Can we be specific about triggers? Which Xid codes are we targeting? Also we need to avoid heavy IO during production drains.

Jon: Agree. Today we capture full dmesg only on node crash. Idea: a compact 'failure snippet' that includes:
- last 200 lines of dmesg (`dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200`)
- `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERROR` output
- `journalctl -k -n 200 --no-pager`
- `nvidia-smi -L` to map UUID -> PCI
Compress and upload to s3 with metadata tags (node,gpu,trigger,xid). Keep snippets small (<=10MB gz).

Alyssa: Sketch of the hook for the node-agent (pseudo):
```bash
# /usr/local/bin/gpu-failure-snippet.sh
EVENT="$1"  # e.g. XID, ECC, DRAIN
OUTDIR=/var/log/gpu-failures/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$HOSTNAME
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"
dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > "$OUTDIR"/dmesg.tail.txt
journalctl -k -n 200 --no-pager > "$OUTDIR"/journal.tail.txt
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERROR > "$OUTDIR"/nvidia-errors.txt 2>&1
 nvidia-smi -L > "$OUTDIR"/gpus.txt
tar -czf "$OUTDIR".tar.gz -C /var/log/gpu-failures $(basename "$OUTDIR")
# push to internal S3 with tags: trigger=$EVENT,node=$HOSTNAME
/opt/logshipper/ship --bucket internal-gpu-snippets --tags "trigger=$EVENT,node=$HOSTNAME" "$OUTDIR".tar.gz
rm -rf "$OUTDIR"
```

Maria: Also include a tiny structured envelope alongside the tarball with these fields: node, gpu_index, gpu_uuid, xid, ecc_uncorrectable_delta, driver_version, kernel_version, timestamp. That will make correlation + indexing easy.

Kevin: Regex ideas for Xid detection in dmesg/journalctl: `(?i)Xid\s*([0-9]+):`  — but we also need alt matches like 'GPU has fallen off the bus' and 'Ecc error' since vendors vary. We'll treat any match as suspect, but include raw snippet so humans can confirm.

Jon: For system integration we can wire a systemd path/unit that triggers the agent when kernel logs contain a matching string. Quick systemd unit example:
```ini
[Unit]
Description=GPU failure snippet trigger

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/gpu-failure-snippet.sh XID

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
We can combine with a small watcher that greps `dmesg -T` and fires only on new matches.

LogShipper-Bot: New pipeline staged: 'gpu-failure-snippets' with 7d retention in dev. Tags available: severity:suspect, trigger:Xid, driver_version. Destination: s3://internal-gpu-snippets/dev.

Alyssa: Two concerns: 1) privacy - scrub kernel cmdline, container IDs, and any env vars from snippets. 2) avoid shipping full container logs by default (that's noisy). We should only attach container stdout/stderr if the process is the GPU driver pid and there is an explicit hotpath.

Maria: Ops note: when draining a node include `nvidia-smi -L` output and PCI bus-id to map noisy card to instance claims. Also capture lspci -vvnn for the slot.

Oncall: If we add this we absolutely need rate-limiting: 1 snippet per GPU per hour per node. Otherwise SSDs fill up and shipper queues blow up during flakey events.

Kevin: :thumbsup: I'll add agent rate-limit logic and a size cap (10MB gz). Also add fallback mode where if compressed size > cap we build a delta file with only 'ERROR'/'Xid' sections to keep keys.

Jon: For parsing/attribution we should add two indexed fields to the envelope: "xid" (numeric or "unknown") and "ecc_uncorrectable_delta" (int). Add a derived metric that increments on any non-zero delta so we can alert on rate spikes. Also consider a small bloom of last 100 error hashes per node to avoid duplicate uploads.

Maria: Plan: Alyssa to PR agent changes; Kevin to update shipper pipeline and retention; Jon to add parsing rules and indexing; Oncall to run canary in us-east-1 next Tue. We'll track T-9281. :rocket:

SRE-Bot: Created task T-9281: gpu-failure-snippet-rollout — assigned to Alyssa, Kevin, Jon — due 2026-03-24.

Kevin: I'll open the shipper PR later today. Can we get a test vector set? If someone can paste a few real dmesg snippets (sanitized) I'll add them to unit tests.

Alyssa: I'll collect two sanitized Xid/ECC examples from last week's incidents and drop them in the PR.

Maria: Thanks all. Small request: add a short runbook blurb for oncall to explain how to fetch and decode the snippet quickly (curl + tar -xz). That reduces context switch.

Oncall: Will do — I'll draft a 5-step blurb and paste in the runbook page.
